analysis:
The supplied units are documentation and changelog only: AGENTS.md (an unchanged-context excerpt at lines 359-480), the new changelog.d/provider-release-version-boundary.md, docs/AGENTS.md (stamp date and the provider version-bump mapping row at head line 182), and docs/developer/build.md (patch only). None of them changes executable code, authorization, attestation, encryption, billing, or the data-exposure paths. The security-relevant claim is in the changelog and build.md: provider packaging and retained-build recovery now validate against ProviderCore.version, the signed release tag and the built binary, and no longer against the coordinator's LatestProviderVersion. The text says signed-source, SDK qualification and immutable-artifact checks remain required.

The actual script and workflow changes (scripts/check-release-version.sh, release workflows, the coordinator LatestProviderVersion display fallback) were not in the supplied units, so the PR's real enforcement cannot be assessed here. A later pass should check three things if those files are in the PR. First, whether decoupling from LatestProviderVersion weakens the release-admission or minimum-version gates that relate to A-011, A-017 and T-034. Second, whether the tag-to-binary binding still rejects a mismatched or downgraded build. Third, whether the retained-build recovery path still verifies the immutable-artifact and signature requirements. No threat-model assumption is invalidated by the documentation text itself. Because the implementing diffs are unreviewed, this is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.
